end.summary:
Practised checking answers by estimating first.
For 48 ÷ 6, Kabir rounded to 50 ÷ 6 and got an estimate of 8; they compared it with the exact answer 8.
For subtraction and addition examples, Kabir rounded to convenient numbers and calculated estimates.
Kabir continued to expect an exact match between the estimate and the exact answer; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Kabir practised rounding numbers before calculating so an answer can be checked for reasonableness. They clearly used 50 ÷ 6 to estimate 48 ÷ 6 and matched the estimate with the exact answer. They mixed up “close to” with “exactly equal,” and this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, ask them to estimate one everyday addition or subtraction and discuss whether the exact answer is close to the estimate rather than identical.
